description:
FILED s458al (agent AL, round 15), measured while probing #840.

cl/pcl-runtime.lisp:

    (defvar |$]| (make-p-box "5.030000") "Perl version number")
    ... :display "v5.30.0")  ;; $^V, "Payload 5.30.0 matches $] = 5.030000."

but everything else in the project targets 5.40: `Pl::Parser::%PCL_FEATURE_BUNDLE`
answers `use v5.40` bundles, `Pl/t/feature-pragma-01.t` re-derives the
thresholds from a 5.40 perl, and #840's `%feature::feature` / `%warnings::Offsets`
are 5.40.3's tables.

CONSEQUENCE MEASURED: the real experimental.pm compares `$]` against
`%min_version` -- with $] = 5.030000 a feature whose minimum is 5.34 would
croak "Need perl 5.34.0 or later" if it ever reached that arm (it does not
for `try`, which is caught by the earlier warnings-category arm; it WOULD for
any feature perl 5.40 has and %warnings::Offsets does not name).

NOT a free edit: `%p-parse-require-version` reads `$]`, so raising it changes
what `use v5.36;` / `use 5.038;` do, and perl-tests / companion rows that
branch on the version move with it.  MEASURE FIRST: grep both populations for
`$]` and `$^V` and count the rows that would flip, then decide.  Related
#870 (version.pm's compare is wrong independently of which number $] holds).
subject: PCL reports $] = 5.030000 / $^V = v5.30.0 while targeting perl 5.40 semantics
